raw_response:
I've farmed these 10 mu for 40 years. Me and my wife handle most of the work ourselves — hiring labor costs too much, and at our age we know every corner of this land anyway. I finished picking the last of my cotton last week, and the maize came off a few days before that. Now it's October 8th, and I'm turning my mind to the winter wheat planting and what the whole year ahead looks like.

I keep about 6 mu in wheat-maize double cropping and the other 4 mu in cotton. The wheat-maize is our stomach crop — we eat some, sell some. Cotton is where the cash comes from, but it's heavy work and the price bounces around. I'm 63 now, not as strong as I used to be, so I have to think hard about labor. My wife and I can still manage, but we pace ourselves.

For the **winter wheat**, I'll plant around October 10th. I'll use that improved Jinmai variety I've been using for five years now — about 15 kg of seed per mu, costing me 35 yuan from the dealer. For fertilizer, the extension technician told me 15 kg of pure nitrogen per mu is enough, but I usually put a little more to be safe. I'll spread 50 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base before planting — that's about 7.5 kg N — and then at jointing in March I'll topdress with 15 kg of urea per mu, which is another 7 kg N. So roughly 14–15 kg N total. I irrigate three times: once right after planting if the soil is dry, once at green-up in spring, and once at heading in May. If it's a drought year like 2019, I'll add a fourth, but three is usually enough. I spray herbicide once after planting, and keep an eye out for aphids in spring. I'm hoping for about 420 kg per mu if the spring rain cooperates.

For **summer maize**, the turnaround after wheat harvest in mid-June is brutally tight — sometimes only three or four days. I hire the combine for wheat harvest to save time, then I plant the maize immediately, often the next morning. I buy hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu at 55 yuan. I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer at planting, and if the plants look pale at the big trumpet stage, I'll side-dress some urea. I irrigate once or twice for maize — summer has some rain, so it doesn't need as much as wheat. One herbicide spray at planting, and that's usually it. I expect around 480 kg per mu if the summer storms don't flatten it.

For **cotton**, I'll plant in late April on the 4 mu. I mix some saved seed with new hybrid seed I buy — about 3 kg per mu, 40 yuan. Cotton needs patience. I put 40 kg of compound as base and topdress with urea at flowering. I irrigate twice, maybe three times. The real cost is pesticide — bollworm is always a threat, so I spray insecticide 3–4 times and herbicide once. Picking is the hard part. With just me and my wife, we pick in rounds through September and October. It wears us out, but cotton pays the bills. I'm hoping for 280 kg per mu of seed cotton.

Money is always tight. Total input costs will run me about 4,600 yuan for the year. I could push for higher yields with more fertilizer, but if I spend too much and the weather turns bad, I'll have no cash left for medicine or emergencies. Better to be a little conservative.
